t: #3638 Maximum Balanced Shipments — Monotonic Stack DP
o: Choose disjoint contiguous subarrays where the last element is strictly less than the subarray's max; maximize the count. Example 1: [2,5,1] and [4,3] → 2. Example 2: [4,4] → 0 (ties don't count). n up to 1e5 calls for better than O(n²).
k: dp[i] = best count using parcels 0..i-1; dp is non-decreasing since parcels may be skipped.
A segment ending at i is balanced iff it contains an element > weight[i]; the latest such element is the nearest previous strictly-greater index.
Taking the NEAREST previous greater element maximizes dp[p] over all valid segment starts, so one stack lookup suffices.

a.n: Approach 1: O(n²) DP over Segment Starts
a.i: For each end i, scan left tracking the running max; whenever max > weight[i], candidate dp[start] + 1. Simple and correct, but quadratic.
s: For each i, walk start from i down to 0 maintaining max.
If max > weight[i], dp[i+1] = max(dp[i+1], dp[start] + 1).
Also carry dp[i+1] = dp[i] (skip parcel i); answer dp[n].
a.t: O(n²) worst case (strictly decreasing prefixes) — fine for moderate n, risky at 1e5.

a.i: Maintain a decreasing stack of indices. For end i, pop indices with weight ≤ weight[i]; whatever remains on top is the nearest index with a strictly greater weight — the best possible segment start, because dp is non-decreasing and any valid segment must contain some greater element, the closest one being at least as good. One O(1) transition per i.
s: Keep a stack of indices with strictly decreasing weights.
For each i, pop while stack top weight ≤ weight[i].
If the stack is non-empty with top p, dp[i+1] = max(dp[i], dp[p] + 1); else dp[i+1] = dp[i].
a.t: O(n) — each index is pushed and popped at most once.
a.sp: O(n) for dp and the stack.

w: The monotonic-stack version hinges on dp being non-decreasing (skipping is free) — verify that before trusting the 'nearest greater is best' shortcut. Pitfalls: strict inequality (equal weights don't balance, as in [4,4]), and off-by-one in dp indexing. Follow-up: maximize total shipped parcels instead of shipment count, or require shipments of length ≥ 2 explicitly.
